How fast buses move on Vermont Avenue, hour by hour since 2016

Every hour of every day for more than ten years, rebuilt from the timetables LA Metro has published, and checked against speeds measured from bus GPS. The corridor runs 11.7 miles from Sunset Boulevard to Athens Station.

What the long series is

LA Metro keeps its bus timetable (GTFS) in a public git repository with versions since 2016. For each date we take the version in force, find every 204 and 754 trip, and time it between cross streets. Metro resets running times at service changes using measured trips, so the timetable follows real conditions with a lag. Stretches where the line stays flat for a year or more are periods when Metro left the running times unchanged; they are not evidence that traffic stood still.

What is measured

  • Cal-ITP (Caltrans) publishes stop-to-stop speeds from archived bus GPS: the middle trip and the 20th to 80th percentile range for one recent weekday.
  • A collector in this project records live GPS positions from Metro's public feed. It has only just started, so the live points cover a single evening.

The archive

hourly records from to , stored as Parquet (one folder per year) with gzipped CSV copies of the corridor rows and a Frictionless datapackage.json describing every column. Raw GPS pings are also exported as Open Mobility Foundation MDS 2.0 Telemetry objects.

Limits to state on stage

  • These are bus speeds including stops, so they sit well below car speeds on the same street.
  • MDS has no transit-bus mode and no roadway-speed table. The telemetry export borrows its vehicle-position format; the hourly table is our own schema.
  • A measured hourly history needs an archive of GPS feeds. That starts now with the collector, or sooner with access to Metro's or Cal-ITP's stored feeds.
